newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended lower following a weaker performance in New York. March lost $3.10 to close at $303.70 per tonne while May gave up $4.0 to close at $303.30. New York saw the expected technical correction but prices ended off the day's lows after late-session bargain-hunting by the trade lifted the spot March contract back towards the middle of the day's range. March ended 15 points lower at 10.71 cents/lb while May shed 13 points to close at 10.76 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 7 and 9 points. Given current bearish fundamentals there should be more room on the downside.

EU - The European Commission on 19 December raised its estimate of 1996/97 beet white sugar production to 15.92 million tonnes, slightly below our own projection of 16.0 million tonnes but up on the previous estimate of 15.58 million tonnes and last year's figure of 15.636 million tonnes. A quota supplies now estimated at 11.279 million tonnes (11.724 million tonnes), B quota supplies at 2.442 million tonnes (2.357 million tonnes) and C sugar supplies at 2.736 million tonnes (2.483 million tonnes). The Commission continue to forecast that producers will carry over as a segregated stock 0.9 million tonnes, leaving 1.836 million tonnes of "C" sugar to be exported compared to the previous estimate of 1.596 million tonnes and last year's figure of 1.636 million tonnes.

Iraq is evaluating over 120 offers from international sugar houses for supplies of two to four cargoes of sugar, but there were no signs of an immediate decision, traders said. Iraq recently said it could import some 300,000 tonnes of sugar over a six-month period when it will be selling oil in exchange for food under a $2 billion deal approved by the UN.
